context.exploration_scope: Tested whether PHASE-SSI-S6's confirmed Principle would be a groundless generalization if applied to a different real goal (goal_semantic_quality) in a different real situation (a taxonomy-reclassification blocker, not an infrastructure blocker) -- the only other real BLOCKED chain, not cherry-picked

problem: PHASE-SSI-S6 confirmed the Principle works correctly on its own goal, but a Principle that has only ever been checked against the situation it was derived from hasn't demonstrated it knows its own boundary -- whether it would silently overreach onto a real but different goal/situation had never been tested against real data.

decision.decision_summary: Precondition check against the only other real BLOCKED chain (goal_semantic_quality, owner_domain="PB taxonomy design (separately-scoped future phase)", action_type="process_redesign") vs the Principle's evidenced precondition (owner_domain="infrastructure (not code, not LPM)", action_type="infra_restoration"): precondition_satisfied=false. independent_verdict=DEFERRED_BY_SCOPE_EXCLUSION, principle_guided_verdict=NOT_APPLICABLE_PRECONDITION_NOT_MET, match=false. A precondition-blind generalization would have concluded "DEFERRED" (coincidentally matching the surface BLOCKED label without matching the real reason) -- shown for contrast, not used as grounds for agreement. Application REFUSED. 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution, 0 real project modifications. Verdict: PRINCIPLE_MISMATCH.

action.action_summary: Fresh-read the Principle and the only other real BLOCKED chain in trace v16, mechanically compared owner_domain/action_type against the Principle's evidenced precondition, computed an independent verdict from the real trace data alone, computed the Principle-guided verdict honestly (precondition-checked, not blindly applied), and compared the two -- explicitly also computing what a precondition-blind generalization would have concluded, to document why a surface-level label match alone would not have been real corroboration.

evidence.evidence_detail: other_goal=goal_semantic_quality, precondition_satisfied=false, verdicts_match=false, final_state=PRINCIPLE_MISMATCH, regression_all_passed=true, dangling=0, duplicates=0

result.note: The Principle's real precondition (external infrastructure blocker) is not met by goal_semantic_quality's real situation (an internal taxonomy-reclassification deferral) -- correctly identified as ungrounded generalization and application was refused, even though a careless surface-level check (both chains are 'BLOCKED') would have looked like a match.

cause.root_cause_summary: Two real chains sharing a surface-level status label (both 'BLOCKED') does not mean they share a cause -- goal_production_runtime is blocked by something genuinely outside this automation's execution boundary (unreachable external GPU hardware), while goal_semantic_quality is blocked by an internal design task that was deliberately scoped out of earlier phases, which this automation could in principle act on. Conflating the two would let a narrow, correctly-scoped Principle silently license inaction on a goal it was never evidenced against.

lesson: A Principle's boundary is only real once it has been checked against a genuinely different real case and shown to correctly refuse (or correctly extend) rather than merely re-confirmed on the case it came from -- and the check has to compare the underlying precondition, not just the surface-level verdict label, or a coincidental label match on two unrelated situations would be mistaken for validation.
